elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.3 lets "A Party ... assign, sell or transfer the whole of its rights and obligations ... to (e) a Subsidiary or Affiliate of that Party; and (d) another Subsidiary or Affiliate of that Party's Parent Company", and the inserted subparagraph expressly carves Teleglobe USA Inc. out of the new consent requirement, so our affiliate route survives consent-free (only the timely written notice in 22.6 applies).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: 22.3(a) permits assignment of the whole of a Party's rights and obligations to "a successor of that Party" without consent; the unqualified word "successor" is at least as broad as merger/acquisition/asset-sale successors and is untouched by the insertion for Teleglobe USA Inc.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The insertion is scope-limited: "Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 and 22.5 do not permit any Party other than Teleglobe USA Inc. to assign ... without the prior written consent of Teleglobe USA Inc." But retained 22.1 permits assignment "Except as otherwise provided in Paragraph 12 and Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 and 22.5" — the Paragraph 12 exception is an independent, untouched no-consent transfer route for other Parties, and Paragraph 12's text is not in the record, so a consent-free counterparty transfer route may remain. Repair by opening the new subparagraph with "Notwithstanding Paragraph 12 and Subparagraphs 22.2 to 22.5 ..." (or otherwise excluding Paragraph 12 transfers by other Parties).

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted language: consent "of Teleglobe USA Inc., which must not be unreasonably withheld"; retained 22.2 also keeps the Management Committee reasonableness standard, so the two operate cumulatively without contradiction.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The bar is drafted absolutely on its face ("no such assignment, sale or transfer may be made to a competitor of Teleglobe USA Inc."), but "such" is tied to assignments under 22.2-22.5 only; a transfer by another Party under the retained Paragraph 12 exception in 22.1 would not be caught, so "never" is not yet achieved. Repair by extending the competitor bar to any assignment, sale or transfer by any other Party under this Agreement, including under Paragraph 12.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "A change of control of Teleglobe USA Inc. does not give any other Party any right to terminate this Agreement or Teleglobe USA Inc.'s participation in it." No retained sentence creates a change-of-control right, so this is a confirming (belt-and-braces) statement with no contradiction.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the insertion, only Teleglobe USA Inc. may use 22.3(a) consent-free; every other Party's successor assignment under 22.2-22.5 now requires our prior written consent, so the mutual successor right required by the fallback is defeated by the drafter's own edit.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.6: "A Party exercising its rights under Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 or 22.5 must give notice in writing to all other Parties in a timely manner."

Retained 22.3(e)/(d), 22.4 and 22.5 leave Teleglobe USA Inc. free to assign to Subsidiaries, Affiliates, Parent Companies and Parent Company subsidiaries without any consent; under the ASSIGN fallback rule any retained no-consent non-successor exception (including this affiliate/parent exception) defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: 22.2 ("The Management Committee must not unreasonably withhold or delay its approval") plus the inserted "must not be unreasonably withheld" standard for our consent.

reasons: Position-incomplete at the preferred level: the new subparagraph disables only Subparagraphs 22.2-22.5 for other Parties, but retained 22.1 also excepts "Paragraph 12" from the general assignment prohibition. That leaves an untouched, potentially consent-free transfer route for counterparties (and one outside the new competitor bar). Fix by drafting the insertion as an override of Paragraph 12 as well, e.g. "Notwithstanding Paragraph 12 and Subparagraphs 22.2, 22.3, 22.4 and 22.5, no Party other than Teleglobe USA Inc. may assign, sell or transfer the whole or any part of its rights or obligations ... without the prior written consent of Teleglobe USA Inc. ...", and extend the competitor prohibition to any such transfer.

Fallback is not available on the current draft either (mutual successor right removed for other Parties by the edit; our own consent-free affiliate/parent exceptions in 22.3-22.5 are retained), so the preferred level must be completed - the Paragraph 12 gap is the single repair needed.
Customer-side preferred elements are genuinely already met (22.3(a) successor; 22.3(d)/(e) affiliate; timely written notice under 22.6) and are correctly preserved rather than cut back.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language or extra procedures; the change-of-control confirmation and the reasonableness standard both sit inside the preferred checklist (note the confirming change-of-control sentence is declaratory only, as no such right exists today).

Intent preserved: the new consent layer is cumulative with 22.2's Management Committee approval rather than contradictory; 22.4's partial-assignment/Schedule mechanics, 22.5's ownership conditions and 22.6's notice duty all survive, and the insertion creates no dangling cross-reference (though it should be given its number, 22.7, in the rendered text).

Confirm on the face of the document that Teleglobe USA Inc. is our client; the redline hard-codes that name as the consent-holder in a multi-Party consortium agreement, and every other Party will read it as a unilateral veto - flag that negotiation exposure in the cover note.
